messages:
marta: Quick check — I'm iterating on the Threshold Preview UI. Two competing patterns: (A) non-modal inline drawer that slides from the right for quick skims, or (B) modal that fully traps focus for edit flows. Also thinking about where to place the small help text for per-channel overrides. Screenshot/frames: https://figma.redwood/threshold-preview (WIP) sam: my 2¢ — accessibility first: if it's a modal, use aria-modal + focus trap and label. If it's a drawer, don't leave keyboard users stranded; focus should land on the first actionable control and return to the trigger on close. Also live updates need an aria-live region so screen readers know preview changed. jin: implementation note — we have an existing Drawer component we can reuse. It currently prevents body scroll but doesn't always trap focus. Trapping is doable but might require refactor. Backdrop-click behavior when there are unsaved edits is a little tricky. alex: product context — research shows people expect the preview to immediately reflect draft changes (even unsaved). We should clearly surface "unsaved edits" state. Also when suppression rules conflict, highlight that in the preview (red outline + tooltip) so users see why a channel won't notify. lili: copy suggestions: change "Per-channel overrides override global thresholds" to "Channel-specific settings take precedence." For the unsaved banner: shorter copy: "Preview shows draft rules — not yet applied." sam: a11y nit — don't rely on color alone to indicate conflicts. Add an icon (⚠️) and programmatic text via aria-describedby. For the live region, something like: ```html
Preview updated
``` is good. Also ensure keyboard focus order: trigger -> first control -> preview list -> close. marta: proposal: use the drawer for quick preview/skimming (non-trapping but focus moves to close button), and escalate to a modal for the full edit path where we trap focus. Add a compact "Unsaved" pill top-right when draft differs from applied rules. Use icons + color + text for conflict state. jin: sounds reasonable. I'll prototype a drawer variant that sets focus to the close button on open and returns focus on close. For the modal edit flow I'll wire up the existing focus-trap util. I can also add keyboard shortcuts for expand/collapse of channel lists. alex: also we need to handle lots-of-channels case — collapse long channel lists with a "Show 12 more" affordance, keyboard-expandable. And show channel badges (email, slack, pager) inline in preview. lili: language nits — avoid the word "override" in user-facing copy; prefer "channel-specific settings" or "channel settings". For the pill label, "Draft" vs "Unsaved" — I prefer "Draft" (less scary). sam: +1 on "Draft". Tests: add a screen reader walkthrough in PR and a tabbable-order test. Also test when many channels are collapsed (focus landing on expand button). marta: :thumbsup: I'll update Figma with the drawer + modal flows, add the ARIA notes and copy choices (Draft pill, channel-specific wording). If no objections, I'll hand off to frontend for a small patch. jin: picking this up in next sprint. Will post a code sandbox for review. deploy-bot: new preview branch created: feat/threshold-preview-a11y — https://git.redwood/feat/threshold-preview-a11y marta: thanks all — will post updated frames and a quick checklist (a11y, copy, collapse behavior) when ready.
